subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of tangent of x² + y² − 2x + 4y = 0 at (3,−1). Also find the equation of the other tangent parallel to it.

insider_note: The two tangents are on opposite sides of the centre, so the parallel one has the same slope and the constant simply changes sign — reaching 2x + y ± 5 = 0 and then picking the sign the given tangent does not use is the fastest finish.

steps.label: Tangent at the given point
steps.margin_note: Two marks. S₁ = 0 is the formula for a tangent AT a point on the circle. Halve the coefficients before substituting.
steps.memory_tip: S₁ = xx₁ + yy₁ + g(x + x₁) + f(y + y₁) + c = 0. Replace one x by x₁ and one y by y₁ everywhere.
lines: The point (3, −1) lies on the circle, since
steps.why: S₁ = 0 gives the tangent only when the point is on the circle, so the check 9 + 1 − 6 − 4 = 0 is worth writing. Each squared term loses one factor to the point: x² becomes xx₁ and 2gx becomes g(x + x₁).
common_mistakes: Using 2g and 2f in S₁ instead of g and f.

steps.label: The parallel tangent
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The ± gives both tangents; one of them is the tangent already found, so the other is the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Tangents with slope m: y + f = m(x + g) ± r√(1 + m²). The ± produces the pair.
lines: y + f = m(x + g) ± r√(1 + m²)
steps.why: A circle has exactly two tangents with any given slope, one on each side of the centre. The formula produces both at once as 2x + y ± 5 = 0; the minus sign is the tangent already found, so the plus sign is the other one.
common_mistakes: Writing y − f = m(x − g) and losing both signs.
Giving 2x + y − 5 = 0 as the answer, which is the tangent already found.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. The book prints one, and it shows the two tangents on opposite sides of the centre.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel tangents come in pairs, one on each side of the centre, and the centre is midway between them.

elements.text: two tangents of the same slope

steps.why: The two tangents with the same slope are the two positions of a line of that slope at distance r from the centre. They lie on opposite sides of C and are the same distance from it, which is why their constants differ only in sign.
common_mistakes: Drawing both tangents on the same side of the circle.
Drawing the second line through the centre rather than touching the circle.
